title: The crowd at the column grows
summary: Word of the fire coal's waking spreads beyond the hill country's own hearths, and people begin coming to Achadh a' Chalbh in tens and then in hundreds to hear the recital said at the column, camping about the stone rather than passing it by.

title: The first shelters built at the column
summary: The crowd that gathers to hear the recital builds the first low walls of turf and hide about Achadh a' Chalbh, taken down again when the telling ends, because no one yet thinks of the column's ground as a place a person lives.

title: Seathan's nephew gives the telling to a crowd
summary: Clann na Ceiste sends a nephew of Seathan's to Achadh a' Chalbh to say the recital naming the fire coal to a hillside of strangers rather than a single hearth, and an old woman of the gathering tells him a story given to a crowd is safe from dying, whatever changes it gathers in the carrying.

title: The shelters at the column rebuilt
summary: The shelters at Achadh a' Chalbh are rebuilt so many times over on the footings of the ones before them that a household coming for the first time can see, in the worn hollows and packed earth, that others have stood there before it and will stand there after.

title: The bag passes to Seathan's great-grandson
summary: The bag holding the rainbow coal, gual bogha-froise, passes down the keeping to the son of Seathan's daughter's husband, who resolves to try the coal in the oak grove at Doire ghlas itself, a ground no keeper of the line is remembered to have brought it to before.

title: The rainbow tried in the grove
summary: A keeper of Clann na Ceiste carries the rainbow coal north to the oak grove at Doire ghlas and sits with it through a night by his own small fire as Diarmad once sat, waiting for any sign the Keeper gave before; the coal lies black and cold among the ash by morning, and the grove answers him nothing.

title: Aoife's child born
summary: Aoife bears a living child after two she has already lost in their first winters, and lets herself believe, when it survives its own first winter thin but breathing steadily, that this one will live to walk; she sews it, for the first time, a coat cut to its own growing rather than one handed down.

title: Aoife's child dies
summary: Aoife's child sickens in the spring and dies quietly in her arms, the third child she has lost and the first she does not hear cry out at the end, so that she says afterward she knew, before she was willing to know it, that this death would not be like the others.

title: The child buried with the sliver of coal
summary: Aoife closes into her dead child's hand the one sliver of the coloured coal her household still keeps, over her husband's mother's objection, and it is buried with the child at the western edge of Tuam Cnoc dhìreach, the only piece of the vein put into the ground with the dead this age.

title: The graves begin to keep a line
summary: The newer graves at Tuam Cnoc dhìreach's western edge begin, without any household deciding it, to be set in a row facing the northern mountains, each new grave drawn to the line the ones before it have already kept, until a household bringing its dead looks for the row before it looks for empty turf.

title: A grave dug round an old swelling
summary: A young man digging his grandfather's grave at Tuam Cnoc dhìreach proposes levelling an old unnamed swelling in his row's path, and is rebuked by an elder digger, who tells him no man may open a grave whose occupant he cannot name; the row bends round it instead.

title: Aoife dies
summary: Aoife dies in her seventieth year, forty years after burying her child, and is carried to Tuam Cnoc dhìreach and laid in the row nearest the western edge where the child already lies, the row bending as it reaches her grave to keep clear of the old swelling beside it.
